findings.message: LockManager.reclaim is declared `async reclaim(threadId: number): Promise<readonly LockInfo[]>`, while the approved contract is synchronous: `(threadId: number) => readonly LockInfo[]`. Because it is async, callers have to await it or attach .catch. watchWorker does the latter (line 787). The LLD expected a synchronous return because a lock holds no native resource. The API shape that the s2 router will consume therefore differs from the approved contract.

errorOf(e: unknown): { name; message } is a test-helper copy of the identical serializer in the store worker helper. Both workers post errors back to the parent thread in the same shape, so a shared test-helper module would keep the two error contracts from drifting apart.

strip(i: LockInfo) has no callers in the graph. It is either dead code left over from an earlier version or a helper whose intended assertion was dropped. Remove it, or wire it into the snapshot comparisons it was written for.

LockManager.reclaim calls 13 separate primitives: the mutex take/unlock, recount, clearPending/clearHolder, bumpVersion, holdersOf/pendingOf, readHolder/readPending, and the slot base helpers. All of this runs under a dead-thread mutex takeover. A dead-worker cleanup routine this dense is the hardest place to check the shared-memory invariants. Splitting the holder sweep from the pending sweep would make each step reviewable. This is based only on the summary's call fan-out, with no confirmed defect.
